items.headline: Regulation lets J&K and Ladakh High Court sit in Ladakh
items.text: The President promulgated the Union Territory of Ladakh (Sitting of Bench of the High Court of Jammu and Kashmir, and Ladakh in Ladakh) Regulation, 2026. It permits the High Court to sit in Ladakh for cases arising there.

items.headline: Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers - Disclosure Scheme Rules, 2026 notified
items.text: The Finance Ministry notified the Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers - Disclosure Scheme Rules, 2026. Eligible taxpayers may disclose undeclared foreign assets on a 60% payment, with a deadline of December 31, 2026.

items.headline: Draft SHANTI Rules, 2026 on nuclear plant licensing released
items.text: The Department of Atomic Energy released the draft Sustainable Harnessing and Advancement of Nuclear Energy for Transforming India (SHANTI) Rules, 2026. They propose a single composite licence for building, operating and decommissioning nuclear plants and five-yearly review of operator liability.

items.headline: Monsoon Session 2026 ends: 12 Bills introduced, 11 passed
items.text: The Monsoon Session of Parliament (July 20 to August 13, 2026) concluded with 12 Bills introduced and 11 passed. Bills passed include the Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026, the Bankers' Books Evidence Bill, 2026 and the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026.

items.headline: Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026 passed; creates National Tribunals Commission
items.text: Parliament passed the Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026, introduced in Lok Sabha on August 10, 2026. It sets up a National Tribunals Commission for selection, performance review and inquiries into conduct of tribunal members, and repeals the Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021.

items.headline: Bankers' Books Evidence Bill, 2026 passed, replacing the 1891 Act
items.text: Parliament passed the Bankers' Books Evidence Bill, 2026, introduced in Lok Sabha on August 3, 2026. It makes electronic banking records admissible as evidence and replaces the Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1891.

items.headline: Parliament passes MMDR Amendment Bill and MSMED Amendment Bill, 2026
items.text: Parliament passed the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, empowering the Centre to regulate mineral-bearing lands and limit State levies. It also passed the MSMED (Amendment) Bill, 2026, letting the Centre notify MSME thresholds and capping mediation at 90 days.

items.headline: Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 passed
items.text: Parliament passed the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 during the Monsoon Session. It exempts FIIs and the Bank for International Settlements from income tax on government securities income and grants exemptions to certain foreign companies.

items.headline: JPC presents report on Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026
items.text: The Joint Parliamentary Committee on the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 (Chair: Sudhir Gupta) presented its report. The Bill amends the Companies Act, 2013 and LLP Act, 2008 on auditor appointments, CSR obligations and NFRA powers.

items.headline: Indian Statistical Institute Bill, 2026 introduced
items.text: The Indian Statistical Institute Bill, 2026 was introduced. It converts ISI from a society into a not-for-profit body corporate, makes the President its Visitor and replaces the Indian Statistical Institute Act, 1959.

items.headline: Parliament passes Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026
items.text: Parliament passed the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026. It increases imprisonment and fines for offences and provides for special fast-track courts that must complete trials within three months.

items.headline: Parliament passes Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026
items.text: Parliament passed the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026, introduced in Lok Sabha on July 27. It extends the Act's protection to the national song, with imprisonment of up to three years for violations.

items.body: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India
items.headline: IRDAI notifies regulations under Sabka Bima Sabki Raksha Act, 2025
items.text: IRDAI notified multiple regulations giving effect to the Sabka Bima Sabki Raksha (Amendment of Insurance Laws) Act, 2025, including frameworks on actuaries, amalgamation and policyholder protection funds.

items.headline: Finance Committee report on Securities Markets Code flags excessive delegation to SEBI
items.text: The Standing Committee on Finance submitted its report on the Securities Markets Code. It observed that delegated legislation should not determine essential legislative policy and recommended clarity on SEBI's delegated powers.

items.headline: RBI draft FEMA rules define FDI as foreign investment of 10% or more
items.text: RBI invited comments on draft Foreign Exchange Management rules. The draft provides that FDI will mean foreign investment of 10% or more in a company or LLP.

items.headline: Monsoon Session 2026 of Parliament begins
items.text: The Monsoon Session of Parliament commenced on July 20, 2026. Bills introduced in July include the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026, the MSMED (Amendment) Bill, 2026 and the Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Bill, 2026.

items.headline: Law Ministry releases draft Advocates (Amendment) Bill to admit foreign-qualified lawyers
items.text: The Ministry of Law and Justice released the draft Advocates (Amendment) Bill, 2026. It would allow foreign-qualified lawyers to be enrolled as advocates on a State roll, with their practice restricted to international commercial arbitration.

items.body: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
items.headline: National Anti-Doping Rules, 2026 notified
items.text: The National Anti-Doping Rules, 2026 were notified, replacing the 2021 provisions. They allow the central government to recognise or set up additional dope-testing laboratories.

items.headline: Zero tolerance for AI-generated fake citations (Pooja Ramesh Singh v. J&K Bank)
items.text: In Pooja Ramesh Singh v. Jammu and Kashmir Bank Ltd. (C.A. No. 11950/2025) the Supreme Court set aside decisions that relied on non-existent case law and declared zero tolerance for citing unverified AI-generated material.

items.body: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
items.headline: Draft National Pharmacy Commission Bill, 2026 released
items.text: The Health Ministry released the draft National Pharmacy Commission Bill, 2026. It proposes a common exit examination for pharmacy licensing and registration to practise.

items.body: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
items.headline: Draft amendments to Medical Devices Rules, 2017 cut licensing timelines
items.text: The Health Ministry released draft amendments to the Medical Devices Rules, 2017 (G.S.R. 515(E)) proposing to shorten approval timelines for manufacturing licences for Class B, C and D devices by 10 to 15 days at each stage. Comments were invited until July 23, 2026.

items.body: Department of Food and Public Distribution
items.headline: Draft National Food Security (Amendment) Bill, 2026 changes Antyodaya entitlements
items.text: The Department of Food and Public Distribution released the draft National Food Security (Amendment) Bill, 2026 to amend the National Food Security Act, 2013. It would change Antyodaya Anna Yojana entitlements from 35 kg per household per month to 7 kg per person per month, capped at 35 kg per household; comments were due by July 13, 2026.

items.headline: Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Rules amended to prescribe purposes and utilisation thresholds
items.text: Amendments to the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Rules, 2011 were notified. They prescribe the purposes for which foreign contributions may be used and require 75% utilisation of earlier funds before further disbursement.

items.body: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
items.headline: Draft Drugs Rules amendment replaces 60% shelf-life rule for imported drugs
items.text: The Health Ministry published draft amendments to the Drugs Rules, 1945 (GSR 505(E)) replacing the requirement of 60% remaining shelf life for imported drugs with a minimum residual shelf life of one year. Stricter requirements are retained for biological products and radiopharmaceuticals; comments were due by July 22, 2026.

items.headline: RBI directions bar dark patterns and forced bundling by regulated entities
items.text: RBI amended its directions on responsible business conduct (on June 15 and 24, 2026). The amendments prohibit dark patterns and compulsory bundling, set customer consent protocols and revise liability rules for fraudulent transactions.

items.headline: FEMA Non-debt Instruments Rules amended to widen investment by individuals abroad
items.text: The Foreign Exchange Management (Non-debt Instruments) Rules, 2019 were amended. The changes extend investment eligibility to individuals resident outside India and raise equity holding limits.

items.headline: Draft rules on adjudicating mining contraventions decriminalised by Jan Vishwas Act, 2026
items.text: The Ministry of Mines released the draft Minerals (Manner of Holding Inquiry and Appeal) Rules, 2026 and the draft Offshore Areas Mineral (Manner of Holding Inquiry and Appeal) Rules, 2026. They prescribe procedures for adjudicating contraventions converted from criminal offences to civil penalties under the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act, 2026, including summary disposal. Comments were due by July 11, 2026.

items.headline: Income-tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026 exempts FIIs and BIS on government securities income
items.text: The Income-tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026 was promulgated. It exempts foreign institutional investors and the Bank for International Settlements from income tax on interest and capital gains from government securities.

items.headline: Coal Exchange Rules, 2026 notified
items.text: The Coal Exchange Rules, 2026 were notified, creating a regulatory framework for electronic coal trading platforms under the oversight of the Coal Controller Organisation.

items.body: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India
items.headline: IBBI amends liquidation regulations, shortens timeline to 180 days
items.text: The IBBI (Liquidation Process) (Fourth Amendment) Regulations, 2026 were notified. They provide for Committee of Creditors supervision of the liquidation process and shorten liquidation timelines to 180 days.

items.headline: Zero coupon zero principal instruments by NPOs added as eligible CSR activity
items.text: Schedule VII of the Companies Act, 2013 and related rules were amended. Subscription to zero coupon zero principal instruments issued by non-profit organisations now counts as corporate social responsibility expenditure.

items.headline: Bihar special intensive revision of electoral rolls upheld (ADR v. Election Commission of India)
items.text: In Association for Democratic Reforms v. Election Commission of India (W.P.(C) No. 640/2025) the Supreme Court upheld the special intensive revision of electoral rolls in Bihar as proportionate and in line with the statute.

items.headline: Draft rules released under VB-G RAM G Act, 2025
items.text: Draft rules were released under the Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025. They specify fund allocation and wage payment mechanisms for the rural employment guarantee.

items.headline: RBI invites comments on draft directions on conduct of loan recovery agents
items.text: RBI sought public comments on draft directions governing the conduct of recovery agents engaged by regulated entities.

items.body: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
items.headline: Draft amendments to National Anti-Doping Act propose criminal penalties for trafficking
items.text: Draft amendments to the National Anti-Doping Act, 2022 were proposed. They would introduce criminal penalties for trafficking in prohibited doping substances and for administering them to athletes.

items.headline: Ordinance raises Supreme Court judge strength from 33 to 37
items.text: The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Ordinance, 2026 was promulgated. It increases the maximum number of Supreme Court judges, other than the Chief Justice, from 33 to 37.
items.why: First expansion of the Supreme Court's sanctioned strength since 2019.

items.headline: Central rules notified under all four labour codes
items.text: The central government notified the Code on Wages (Central) Rules, the Industrial Relations Code (Central) Rules, the Social Security Code (Central) Rules and the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code (Central) Rules. This operationalises the central framework under the four labour codes.

items.body: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
items.headline: Central Motor Vehicles (Sixth Amendment) Rules, 2026 notified
items.text: The Central Motor Vehicles (Sixth Amendment) Rules, 2026 were notified. They modify vehicle testing protocols and the eligibility criteria for owning automated testing stations.

items.headline: FEMA rules amended to allow 100% foreign investment in Indian insurers
items.text: The Foreign Exchange Management (Non-debt Instruments) (Second Amendment) Rules, 2026 removed the 74% cap on foreign investment in the insurance sector. Full foreign ownership of Indian insurance companies is now permitted.

items.headline: Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Rules, 2026 notified
items.text: The central government notified the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Rules, 2026 under the 2025 Act. The Rules specify the composition of the Online Gaming Authority and the factors for determining whether a game is an online money game.

items.headline: RBI releases draft Master Directions on Prepaid Payment Instruments, 2026
items.text: RBI issued draft Master Directions on Prepaid Payment Instruments, 2026. The draft restricts cross-border transactions, lowers the monthly cash-loading limit for full-KYC PPIs to Rs 10,000 and introduces a Rs 25,000 limit on person-to-person transfers.

items.headline: Budget Session 2026 ends with six Bills passed, including IBC and Jan Vishwas amendments
items.text: The Budget Session (January 28 to April 18, 2026) concluded. Bills passed include the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill, 2026, the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Bill, 2026, the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (Amendment) Bill, 2025, the Industrial Relations Code (Amendment) Bill, 2026, the CAPF (General Administration) Bill, 2026 and the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation (Amendment) Bill, 2026.

items.body: Securities and Exchange Board of India
items.headline: SEBI amends AIF Regulations to cut minimum social impact fund investment to Rs 1,000
items.text: SEBI notified the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Alternative Investment Funds) (Amendment) Regulations, 2026. The minimum investment per investor in social impact funds is reduced from Rs 2,00,000 to Rs 1,000.

items.headline: Lok Sabha votes down Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill on delimitation and seat expansion
items.text: The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, which sought to raise the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha to 850 and enable delimitation on 2011 census data, was defeated in Lok Sabha. The linked Delimitation Bill, 2026 and Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 consequently became infructuous.
items.why: A rare defeat of a constitutional amendment Bill.

items.body: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
items.headline: National Highways Fee rules amended to introduce graduated overload fees
items.text: The National Highways Fee (Determination of Rates and Collection) Fourth Amendment Rules, 2026 were notified. They provide for overload fees graded according to the percentage by which a vehicle exceeds its permitted weight.

items.headline: Ministry of Coal issues guidelines on mining plans for underground coal gasification
items.text: The Ministry of Coal released guidelines requiring mining plans approved by the Coal Controller Organisation for all coal and lignite blocks proposed for underground coal gasification. Plans must include safety management covering subsidence and contamination, a 500-metre barrier from other mining operations, and mine closure plans backed by escrow funds.

items.body: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
items.headline: Draft Tar-balls Management Rules, 2026 released under Environment (Protection) Act
items.text: The Environment Ministry released the draft Tar-balls Management Rules, 2026 under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986. The draft sets a lifecycle management framework for tar-balls, the weathered by-products of oil spills, and assigns institutional responsibilities.

items.body: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs
items.headline: SEZ units allowed to sell in domestic market at concessional customs duty
items.text: CBIC notified concessional customs duty rates allowing eligible manufacturing units in Special Economic Zones to sell goods in the Domestic Tariff Area between April 1, 2026 and March 31, 2027. The benefit is subject to minimum value addition of 20% and a cap linked to 30% of the unit's earlier export value.

items.body: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
items.headline: Draft IT Rules Second Amendment, 2026 would bind intermediaries to Ministry advisories
items.text: MeitY invited comments until April 14, 2026 on draft IT Rules second amendment. It requires intermediaries to comply with written Ministry clarifications and advisories, and extends digital media rules to news and current affairs content shared by users.

items.headline: Mineral Auction and Mineral Concession Rules amended
items.text: Amendments notified to the Mineral (Auction) Rules, 2015 exempt critical minerals below 10% of block value from auction premium and allow forest area exclusion. Amendments to the Minerals Concession Rules, 2016 allow additional minerals in existing leases, with a 60-day State decision.

items.headline: Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 introduced
items.text: The FCRA Amendment Bill, 2026 provides that assets created from foreign contribution of cancelled or surrendered registrations vest provisionally, and then permanently, in a Designated Authority if fresh registration is not obtained within the prescribed time.

items.headline: SC upholds Clause 3 of Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950 on religion
items.text: The Supreme Court upheld Clause 3 of the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950, which limits Scheduled Caste status to persons professing Hinduism, Sikhism or Buddhism. Conversion to another religion results in loss of SC status.

items.headline: Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 introduced, referred to Joint Committee
items.text: The Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 decriminalises offences in favour of civil penalties, raises small company limits to Rs 20 crore capital and Rs 200 crore turnover, and permits conversion of trusts into LLPs. It was referred to a Joint Committee.

items.body: Securities and Exchange Board of India
items.headline: SEBI approves High-Level Committee norms on conflicts of interest of its members
items.text: SEBI approved recommendations of its High-Level Committee on conflict of interest. The Chairman and whole-time members must liquidate or freeze equity investments, with disclosure obligations extending to spouses and dependents.

items.headline: Civil Aviation Ministry issues passenger facilitation directions: 60% seats free of charge
items.text: The Ministry of Civil Aviation directed airlines to allot 60% of seats on every flight free of charge, seat passengers on the same PNR together, publish equipment carriage policies and prominently display passenger rights on delays and cancellations.

items.headline: SC: adoptive mothers entitled to 12 weeks' maternity leave regardless of child's age
items.text: The Supreme Court held that adoptive mothers are entitled to 12 weeks of paid maternity leave irrespective of the age of the adopted child. It struck down the age-linked provision of the Code on Social Security, 2020 as violating Articles 14 and 21.

items.body: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
items.headline: National Highways Fee Rules amended: double toll for unpaid user fee
items.text: Amendments to the National Highways Fee Rules, effective March 17, 2026, define unpaid user fee and impose a double-toll penalty, waived if paid within 72 hours. Dues are recorded in VAHAN after 15 days and notices issued electronically.

items.headline: Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill, 2026 introduced; passed later in March
items.text: Introduced on March 13, 2026 and passed during the Budget Session, the Bill amends the 2019 Act. It changes the definition of transgender person, requires a medical board recommendation for identity certificates, and adds offences with enhanced penalties.

items.headline: Select Committee reports on Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Bill, 2026
items.text: The Select Committee report on the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Bill, 2026 was presented on March 13. The Bill amends 80 central Acts to decriminalise offences, remove imprisonment terms, raise fines by 10% every three years and provide for improvement notices and warnings.

items.headline: Draft Electricity (Rights of Consumers) Amendment Rules, 2026 defer Time-of-Day tariffs
items.text: The draft Rules push Time-of-Day tariffs to April 1, 2027 for commercial and industrial consumers and April 1, 2028 for others, introduce progressive net metering charges (waived for rooftop solar up to 5 kW) and mandate automatic review of abnormal bills.

items.headline: Withdrawal of life support permitted (Harish Rana v. Union of India)
items.text: In Harish Rana v. Union of India (MA 2238/2025 in SLP(C) No. 18225/2024) the Supreme Court permitted withdrawal of clinically assisted nutrition and hydration for a patient in a permanent vegetative state.

items.headline: RBI amends capital market exposure directions, permits acquisition financing
items.text: The RBI issued amendment directions on banks' capital market exposure, effective April 1, 2026, permitting acquisition financing and expanded securities lending. It also invited comments on draft directions allowing commercial banks to lend to listed REITs.

items.headline: Industrial Relations Code (Amendment) Bill, 2026 introduced and passed by both Houses
items.text: The Industrial Relations Code (Amendment) Bill, 2026, introduced on February 11, was passed by both Houses in the first half of the Budget Session. It amends the Industrial Relations Code, 2020 to clarify that three Acts stand repealed with effect from November 21, 2025.

items.headline: Expert committee on sensitivity in sexual offence cases (In Re: Allahabad HC order of 17.03.2025)
items.text: In its suo motu case on the Allahabad High Court order of 17 March 2025 (SMW(Crl) No. 1/2025) the Supreme Court constituted an expert committee to frame guidelines on a sensitive and compassionate judicial approach in sexual offence cases.

items.headline: Limitation Act applies to land acquisition appeals (Deputy Commissioner v. S.V. Global Mill)
items.text: In The Deputy Commissioner v. M/s S.V. Global Mill Limited (C.A. No. 909-910/2026) the Supreme Court held that Section 5 of the Limitation Act applies to appeals under Section 74 of the Right to Fair Compensation Act, 2013.

items.headline: RBI issues draft revised master direction on credit derivatives
items.text: The RBI released a draft revised master direction on credit derivatives. The framework would enable total return swaps and credit default swaps on corporate bonds.

items.body: Securities and Exchange Board of India
items.headline: SEBI consults on ease of doing business measures for REITs and InvITs
items.text: SEBI released a consultation paper proposing regulatory measures to ease doing business for Real Estate Investment Trusts and Infrastructure Investment Trusts.

items.headline: Offshore Areas Mineral (Prevention of Illegal Mining and Transportation) Rules, 2026 notified
items.text: Rules to prevent illegal mining and transport of minerals in offshore areas were notified under the Offshore Areas Mineral (Development and Regulation) Act, 2002.

items.headline: Draft OSH Code regulations issued for metalliferous mines and dock workers
items.text: The Labour Ministry invited comments on draft regulations under the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 for metalliferous mines (released February 4) and dock workers (released February 9). Comments were due by March 21 and March 26, 2026.

items.body: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
items.headline: Draft amendments to New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019 released
items.text: Comments were invited until March 4, 2026 on draft amendments to the New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019. The draft requires notification of changes made to drug products.

items.headline: Union Budget 2026-27 presented in Parliament
items.text: The Union Budget 2026-27 was presented on February 1, 2026, with total expenditure estimated at Rs 53,47,315 crore and a fiscal deficit target of 4.3% of GDP. The first half of the Budget Session ended on February 13.

items.headline: Supreme Court stays UGC (Promotion of Equity in Higher Education Institutions) Regulations, 2026
items.text: In Mritunjay Tiwari v. Union of India, the Supreme Court stayed implementation of the UGC (Promotion of Equity in Higher Education Institutions) Regulations, 2026, about two weeks after their release. The Court said some provisions suffered from ambiguities and could be misused.

items.headline: Budget Session 2026 begins with President's address to joint sitting
items.text: Parliament's Budget Session began on January 28, 2026 with the President addressing a joint sitting of both Houses. The Union Budget was scheduled for presentation on February 1, 2026.

items.body: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
items.headline: Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 notified, extending to rural local bodies
items.text: MoEFCC notified the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, effective April 1, 2026. They extend to rural local bodies and widen the definition of bulk waste generators to include premises of at least 20,000 sq m or using 40,000 litres of water a day.

items.body: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade
items.headline: DPIIT proposes Designs Act, 2000 amendments to protect virtual designs and GUIs
items.text: DPIIT invited comments until February 22, 2026 on a concept note to amend the Designs Act, 2000. It proposes protection for virtual designs, graphical user interfaces and animated characters, and India's accession to the Riyadh Design Law Treaty and Hague Agreement.

items.body: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
items.headline: Uniform consent guidelines under Air and Water Acts amended
items.text: The uniform consent guidelines under the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981 and Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 were amended. Changes extend consent validity and allow verification by environmental auditors.

items.headline: Draft amendments to Mineral (Auction) Rules, 2015 allow partial lease execution
items.text: The Ministry of Mines invited comments until February 23, 2026 on draft amendments to the Mineral (Auction) Rules, 2015. They would allow partial execution of mining leases and let preferred bidders exclude forest portions from blocks.

items.body: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
items.headline: Environment (Protection) Fund Rules, 2026 notified
items.text: MoEFCC notified the Environment (Protection) Fund Rules, 2026. Penalties under the Air Act, 1981, Water Act, 1974 and Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 will be credited to the fund, to be used for monitoring, laboratories and pollution prevention.

items.body: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
items.headline: Emission intensity targets extended to refineries, petrochemicals, textiles and secondary aluminium
items.text: The Greenhouse Gases Emission Intensity Target (Amendment) Rules, 2025 extend the emission intensity framework to four more industries: secondary aluminium, petroleum refineries, petrochemicals and textiles.

items.body: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
items.headline: National Sports Governance (National Sports Bodies) Rules, 2026 released
items.text: The Sports Ministry released the National Sports Governance (National Sports Bodies) Rules, 2026 under the National Sports Governance Act, 2025. They set the procedure for inducting Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit and grounds for disqualification.

items.body: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
items.headline: National Sports Board (Search-cum-Selection Committee) Rules, 2026 released
items.text: The National Sports Board (Search-cum-Selection Committee) Rules, 2026 specify the composition of the Board and the procedure for selecting its members under the National Sports Governance Act, 2025.
